message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | State at STP | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (1 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14 K) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 22.71 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (Cp) |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.025 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.0005 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard entropy (gas) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (non‑polar) |
| | Polarizability | 0.666 Å³ |
| | Van der Waals radius | 1.20 Å |
| | Covalent radius | 31 pm |
| | Atomic radius | 37 pm |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Common oxidation state in compounds | +1 (e.g., H₂O, HCl) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Bond length (H–H) | 0.74 Å |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (UV, visible, IR) |
| | Magnetic moment | 1.410 µB (proton) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic resonance | NMR (¹H), MRI (clinical imaging) |
| | Isotopic abundance | ¹H ≈ 99.98 %, ²H ≈ 0.02 % |
| | Radioactivity | ³H (half‑life 12.32 y) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very low (≈0.1 g L⁻¹ in ethanol) |
| | Flame color | Blue (hydrogen flame) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH = –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electrochemical potential (vs SHE) | 0 V (standard hydrogen electrode) |
| | Redox behavior | Acts as reducing agent (H⁺ + e⁻ → ½ H₂) |
| | Chemical reactivity | Highly reactive as a radical (H•) in combustion, polymerization, etc. |
| | Physical state changes | Forms solid ice at –259 °C, liquid at –252 °C, gas above –252 °C |
| | Pressure–temperature phase diagram | Triple point at 13.99 K, 0.0002 MPa; critical point at 33.19 K, 1.3 MPa |
| | Quantum properties | Exhibits Bose–Einstein condensation in ¹H at ~0.2 K; deuterium forms a quantum solid at low T |
| | Applications | Fuel cells (H₂ + O₂ → H₂O), MRI contrast agents (¹H), hydrogen storage, semiconductor doping, etc. |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive).
- **Non‑polar**: No permanent dipole moment; behaves as a simple diatomic gas.
- **High reactivity**: Forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals, and fuels with oxygen.
- **Electrochemical standard**: The standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) defines the zero of the electrochemical potential scale.
- **Medical imaging**: ¹H NMR is the basis of MRI, making hydrogen the most imaged element in the body.
- **Energy carrier**: Hydrogen fuel cells convert chemical energy to electricity with only water as by‑product.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
